newsitem.title: USA: Yahoo! and Amazon.com sign Web book services deal. [CORRECTED 00:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Yahoo! and Amazon.com sign Web book services deal. [CORRECTED 00:45 GMT]

text.p: Internet media company Yahoo! Inc. and Web bookseller Amazon.com said Monday they have penned an agreement under which Amazon.com will be the premier bookseller featured on Yahoo!

The companies said they will offer users direct links related to Amazon.com book titles from every Yahoo! search result and book category page in a deal which combines the Web navigation guide with the largest online bookseller.

Shares of Yahoo! rose $4.25, or nearly 13 percent, to close at $37.75 on the Nasdaq market, or just slightly short of its 52-week high of $39.38 (corrects from $49.38). Amazon shares gained $1.06, or roughly five percent, to $24 (corrects from $22.94).

Analysts said the deal provides further evidence of the growing importance of the most frequently visited sites on the World Wide Web in attracting traffic -- often discribed as individuals' "eyeballs" -- to their sites.
"First they were selling access to eyeballs and now they're selling access to wallets," Steve Harmon, senior investment analyst at Mecklermedia Corp., said of Yahoo!
Amazon.com calls itself the "Earth's Biggest Bookstore," with a catalog of some 2.5 million titles, Web-based credit card payment and direct shipment to its customers.

Amazon.com has attracted the attention of the publishing industry giants. In the week in May when it launched its initial public offering of stock, Barnes & Noble, Inc. launched its own Web site and filed a lawsuit contesting Amazon.com's claims to being the biggest in the world.
Executives of Yahoo! and Amazon.com said the partnership will enable the bookseller to extend its distribution to a broader audience on the Internet.

"This agreement furthers our strategy of providing customers with as many possible points of access to our store and our vast selection of 2.5 million titles," Amazon.com chief executive Jeff Bezos said in a statement.

The new service, due to be launched this autumn, is designed to offer users the opportunity to review and purchase book titles from Amazon.com. It will initially be integrated throughout the Yahoo! site and its 11 metropolitan services.
Amazon.com will also receive what it said would be "extensive promotional exposure" throughout Yahoo!, including banner advertizing and relevant keyword placement.
